source.title: Neurocomputational mechanisms of prosocial learning and links to empathy.
source.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

confidence_rationale: Shows people can learn to obtain rewards for another person with the same reinforcement-learning algorithm as for self, but more slowly, and that a posterior sgACC/basal forebrain region carries a prediction error only in the prosocial condition. So the algorithm is shared while at least one neural node is other-specific. Held at 0.5 because it is a one-step bandit (no planning at all), so it speaks to the same-machinery question but not to the planned-vs-greedy question MECH-479 poses.
failure_signatures: A prosocial-selective sgACC prediction error in a bandit task shows other-specific VALUATION, not other-specific or shared PLANNING; reading it either way for MECH-479 over-extends it.
Slower prosocial learning could reflect motivation (trait empathy predicts it) rather than a representational limit.

mapping.source_claim_statement: People learn to obtain rewards for others more slowly than for themselves; posterior sgACC/basal forebrain signals a prosocial prediction error only in the prosocial context, and its selectivity and learning speed scale with trait empathy.
mapping.ree_translation: Evidence that benefit for another agent is learned through an RL-shaped signal but routed through a distinct, other-specific node. For REE this suggests that other-agent benefit_exposure may need its own value/error channel feeding the planner, rather than being a relabelled copy of the self channel.
mapping.mapping_caveat: A one-step probabilistic choice task: no trajectory, no lookahead, no accumulation of the other's state. It is silent on whether the hippocampal planned pathway is required.
mapping.source_context: fMRI, probabilistic reward learning for self / other person / no one; RL model fitting; trait empathy correlations.

confidence_components.notes: Clean design, well-cited; bears on shared vs distinct machinery, not on planning horizon.
